messages:
maya: heads-up — saw a customer hit weird backups. requests with both X-Region and X-RouteHints ended up routed to a tiny backup model under high load. route match seemed to prefer the routehint and ignored tenant quota lane. any ideas? :thinking_face:

kevin: which gateway version and can you paste headers (sanitized)?

maya: gateway 1.12.3. sample headers:

```
X-RouteHints: region=us-west;pref=latency
X-Region: us-west-2
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
X-Tenant: acme
```

rafi: we shipped a change to matching order last month that gives header-based routes higher precedence to reduce p99. that might be biting us — it can short-circuit tenant-affinity when both match.

aisha: hmm — we have two concerns: correctness (tenant quota/priority) and caller intent (route hints). i don't love adding a flat override header that lets callers bypass quotas. proposal: add opt-in header `x-rd-prefer-tenant=true` which preserves tenant lane even if a header route matches. default = false.

kevin: agree on opt-in. but also we need a safety net if tenant lane is capacity-constrained. customer here had burst and their tenant lane dropped to <10% capacity so we fell back to backup model. question: do we prefer locality (header) or tenant guarantees?

maya: customer SDK injects X-RouteHints for latency locality, they didn't set prefer-tenant. behavior i want: if tenant lane capacity is degraded, prefer locality route only if it's marked as "explicit override" by customer; otherwise prefer tenant lane and trigger a soft-degrade to avoid cold backup model.

ops-bot: @channel circuit-breaker-bot event: cb:tenant:acme trip_count=3 threshold=3 window=60s status=TRIPPED :warning:

rafi: technical idea: attach a routing metadata tag `degrade_reason=header_interleave` when we choose a backup model because a header route beat tenant-affinity under low-capacity. surface that in logs/metrics.

maya: yes — console needs that tag for rollout UX. if product can filter rollout by `fallback_cause=header_vs_capacity` that's huge for debugging.

kevin: telemetry plan: emit a boolean metric `fallback_via_header` per-request and a histogram `fallback_latency_delta_ms`. alert if `fallback_via_header` > 1% over 5m for any tenant. also add a dashboard facet for `route_decision_trace` showing the ordered predicates.

aisha: implementation sketch: matcher precedence becomes: (explicit override header) > tenant-affinity (if tenant lane healthy) > header-route > region-local. plus a "soft-shed" policy: when tenant lane < X% capacity, try tenant-affinity but return a 202 + `x-rd-fallback-hint` if eventual model would be backup (allowing caller to retry or degrade UX).

maya: can we also emit sample trace tag `x-rd-trace-sample` so ops + evals can replay failing traces? small-sample to avoid overhead.

kevin: yes — add `x-rd-trace-sample: <uuid>` and log it in the route decision. will wire to traces in console.

maya: SG. i'll write a short RFC and a 1.12.4 patch: modify matcher ordering, add opt-in header, emit `degrade_reason` tags, and telemetry. pinging @eng-runtime for perf/semantics review. :eyes:

eng-runtime: quick comment — adding extra decision tags is cheap, but watch memory churn on high QPS. prefer sampling of full decision traces and emit lightweight counters for every request.

maya: noted. thanks all — starting RFC now. :thumbsup:
